questions.text: Let the focal chord PQ of the parabola $y^2=4x$ make an angle of $60^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis, where P lies in the first quadrant. If the circle, whose one diameter is PS, S being the focus of the parabola, touches the $y$-axis at the point $(0, \alpha)$, then $5\alpha^2$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
S is $(1,0)$. Take $P=(t^2, 2t)$; the slope of SP is $\dfrac{2t}{t^2-1}=\sqrt3$, so $\sqrt3t^2-2t-\sqrt3=0$ and, with $t>0$, $t=\sqrt3$. Thus $P=(3, 2\sqrt3)$.
The circle on PS as diameter has centre $(2, \sqrt3)$ and radius $\dfrac{PS}{2}=\dfrac{t^2+1}{2}=2$, which equals the distance of the centre from the $y$-axis, so it touches the $y$-axis at $(0, \sqrt3)$.
$\alpha^2=3$, so $5\alpha^2=15$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $z$ be a complex number such that $|z|=1$. If $\dfrac{2+k^2z}{k+\bar{z}}=kz$, $k\in\mathbf{R}$, then the maximum distance of $k+ik^2$ from the circle $|z-(1+2i)|=1$ is :
questions.sol:
Cross-multiplying: $2+k^2z=k^2z+kz\bar z=k^2z+k$ (since $z\bar z=1$), so $k=2$.
The point is $k+ik^2=2+4i$. Its distance from the centre $1+2i$ is $\sqrt{1^2+2^2}=\sqrt5$.
Maximum distance from the circle $=\sqrt5+1$.

questions.text: If $\theta\in[-2\pi, 2\pi]$, then the number of solutions of $2\sqrt{2}\cos^2\theta+\left(2-\sqrt{6}\right)\cos\theta-\sqrt{3}=0$, is equal to :
questions.sol:
Discriminant $=(2-\sqrt6)^2+8\sqrt6=10+4\sqrt6=(2+\sqrt6)^2$.
$\cos\theta=\dfrac{-(2-\sqrt6)\pm(2+\sqrt6)}{4\sqrt2}$, i.e. $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2}$ or $\cos\theta=-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$.
Each value of $\cos\theta$ (strictly between $-1$ and $1$) is taken twice in every interval of length $2\pi$, so 4 times in $[-2\pi, 2\pi]$.
Total $=4+4=8$.

questions.text: If S and S$^\prime$ are the foci of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{18}+\dfrac{y^2}{9}=1$ and P be a point on the ellipse, then $\min(\mathrm{SP}\cdot\mathrm{S^\prime P})+\max(\mathrm{SP}\cdot\mathrm{S^\prime P})$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$a^2=18$, $b^2=9$, so $e^2=\dfrac12$.
For $P=(x, y)$: $\mathrm{SP}=a+ex$, $\mathrm{S^\prime P}=a-ex$, so $\mathrm{SP}\cdot\mathrm{S^\prime P}=a^2-e^2x^2=18-\dfrac{x^2}{2}$ with $0\le x^2\le18$.
Maximum $18$ (at $x=0$), minimum $18-9=9$ (at $x^2=18$). Sum $=27$.

questions.text: Let ABCD be a tetrahedron such that the edges AB, AC and AD are mutually perpendicular. Let the areas of the triangles ABC, ACD and ADB be 5, 6 and 7 square units respectively. Then the area (in square units) of the $\Delta$BCD is equal to :
questions.sol:
Take A as origin with $\vec{AB}=b\hat i$, $\vec{AC}=c\hat j$, $\vec{AD}=d\hat k$.
Area of BCD $=\dfrac12\left|\vec{BC}\times\vec{BD}\right|=\dfrac12\left|cd\,\hat i+bd\,\hat j+bc\,\hat k\right|$.
So $(\text{area BCD})^2=\left(\dfrac{cd}{2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{bd}{2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{bc}{2}\right)^2=6^2+7^2+5^2=110$.
Area $=\sqrt{110}$.

questions.text: The largest $n\in\mathbf{N}$ such that $3^n$ divides $50!$ is :
questions.sol:
Count the factors of 3 in $1\cdot2\cdots50$: multiples of 3 give $\left[\dfrac{50}{3}\right]=16$, multiples of 9 give a further $\left[\dfrac{50}{9}\right]=5$, multiples of 27 a further $\left[\dfrac{50}{27}\right]=1$.
$n=16+5+1=22$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: For $\alpha, \beta, \gamma\in\mathbf{R}$, if $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\frac{x^2\sin\alpha x+(\gamma-1)e^{x^2}}{\sin2x-\beta x}=3$, then $\beta+\gamma-\alpha$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
The denominator tends to 0, so the numerator must too: $\gamma-1=0$, $\gamma=1$.
The numerator is then $x^2\sin\alpha x\approx\alpha x^3$. The denominator is $(2-\beta)x-\dfrac{4}{3}x^3+\cdots$; for a finite non-zero limit we need $\beta=2$.
Limit $=\dfrac{\alpha}{-4/3}=3$, so $\alpha=-4$.
$\beta+\gamma-\alpha=2+1+4=7$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the function $f(x)=2x^3-9ax^2+12a^2x+1$, where $a>0$, attains its local maximum and local minimum values at p and q, respectively, such that $p^2=q$, then $f(3)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$f^\prime(x)=6x^2-18ax+12a^2=6(x-a)(x-2a)$. With $a>0$, $f^\prime$ changes from $+$ to $-$ at $x=a$ and from $-$ to $+$ at $x=2a$, so $p=a$, $q=2a$.
$a^2=2a$ gives $a=2$, so $f(x)=2x^3-18x^2+48x+1$.
$f(3)=54-162+144+1=37$.

questions.text: The number of sequences of ten terms, whose terms are either 0 or 1 or 2, that contain exactly five 1s and exactly three 2s, is equal to :
questions.sol:
The sequence has five 1s, three 2s and therefore two 0s.
Number of arrangements $=\dfrac{10!}{5!\,3!\,2!}=2520$.

questions.text: Let one focus of the hyperbola H: $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ be at $\left(\sqrt{10}, 0\right)$ and the corresponding directrix be $x=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{10}}$. If $e$ and $l$ respectively are the eccentricity and the length of the latus rectum of H, then $9(e^2+l)$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$ae=\sqrt{10}$ and $\dfrac{a}{e}=\dfrac{9}{\sqrt{10}}$; multiplying, $a^2=9$, so $a=3$ and $e=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}{3}$, $e^2=\dfrac{10}{9}$.
$b^2=a^2(e^2-1)=1$, so $l=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac23$.
$9(e^2+l)=10+6=16$.

questions.text: If $\vec{a}$ is a nonzero vector such that its projections on the vectors $2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$, $\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ and $\hat{k}$ are equal, then a unit vector along $\vec{a}$ is :
questions.sol:
Let $\vec a=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k$. The first two vectors have magnitude 3 and $\hat k$ has magnitude 1, so
$\dfrac{2x-y+2z}{3}=\dfrac{x+2y-2z}{3}=z$.
This gives $x-3y+4z=0$ and $2x-y-z=0$. From the second, $y=2x-z$; substituting, $-5x+7z=0$, so $z=\dfrac{5x}{7}$ and $y=\dfrac{9x}{7}$.
$\vec a\parallel 7\hat i+9\hat j+5\hat k$, magnitude $\sqrt{155}$; of the options, the unit vector is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{155}}(7\hat i+9\hat j+5\hat k)$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let A be the set of all functions $f:\mathbf{Z}\to\mathbf{Z}$ and R be a relation on A such that $R=\{(f, g): f(0)=g(1) \text{ and } f(1)=g(0)\}$. Then R is :
options: Reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
Symmetric but neither reflective nor transitive
Transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric
Symmetric and transitive but not reflective
questions.sol:
Reflexive would need $f(0)=f(1)$ for every $f$, which fails (e.g. $f(x)=x$). Not reflexive.
If $f(0)=g(1)$ and $f(1)=g(0)$, then $g(0)=f(1)$ and $g(1)=f(0)$, so $(g, f)\in R$. Symmetric.
If $(f, g), (g, h)\in R$ then $f(0)=g(1)=h(0)$ and $f(1)=g(0)=h(1)$, which does not give $f(0)=h(1)$; e.g. $f=h=x$, $g=1-x$ gives $(f, g), (g, f)\in R$ but $(f, f)\notin R$. Not transitive.
So R is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive.

questions.text: Let the vertices Q and R of the triangle PQR lie on the line $\dfrac{x+3}{5}=\dfrac{y-1}{2}=\dfrac{z+4}{3}$, QR $=5$ and the coordinates of the point P be $(0, 2, 3)$. If the area of the triangle PQR is $\dfrac{m}{n}$ then :
questions.sol:
The line passes through $A(-3, 1, -4)$ with direction $\vec d=(5, 2, 3)$, $|\vec d|=\sqrt{38}$.
$\vec{AP}=(3, 1, 7)$ and $\vec{AP}\times\vec d=(-11, 26, 1)$, of magnitude $\sqrt{798}$.
Distance of P from the line $=\dfrac{\sqrt{798}}{\sqrt{38}}=\sqrt{21}$.
Area $=\dfrac12\times5\times\sqrt{21}=\dfrac{5\sqrt{21}}{2}=\dfrac mn$, so $2m=5\sqrt{21}\,n$, i.e. $2m-5\sqrt{21}\,n=0$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a twice differentiable function such that $(\sin x\cos y)\left(f(2x+2y)-f(2x-2y)\right)=(\cos x\sin y)\left(f(2x+2y)+f(2x-2y)\right)$, for all $x, y\in\mathbf{R}$. If $f^\prime(0)=\dfrac12$, then the value of $24f^{\prime\prime}\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)$ is :
questions.sol:
Collect terms: $f(2x+2y)(\sin x\cos y-\cos x\sin y)=f(2x-2y)(\sin x\cos y+\cos x\sin y)$, i.e. $f(2x+2y)\sin(x-y)=f(2x-2y)\sin(x+y)$.
With $u=x+y$, $v=x-y$: $\dfrac{f(2u)}{\sin u}=\dfrac{f(2v)}{\sin v}$ for all $u, v$, so $f(t)=c\sin\dfrac t2$.
$f^\prime(0)=\dfrac c2=\dfrac12$ gives $c=1$, so $f(t)=\sin\dfrac t2$ and $f^{\prime\prime}(t)=-\dfrac14\sin\dfrac t2$.
$24f^{\prime\prime}\left(\dfrac{5\pi}{3}\right)=-6\sin\dfrac{5\pi}{6}=-3$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $a\in\mathbf{R}$ and A be a matrix of order $3\times3$ such that $\det(A)=-4$ and $A+I=\begin{bmatrix}1&a&1\\2&1&0\\a&1&2\end{bmatrix}$, where I is the identity matrix of order $3\times3$. If $\det\left((a+1)\,\mathrm{adj}((a-1)A)\right)$ is $2^m3^n$, $m, n\in\{0, 1, 2, \ldots, 20\}$, then $m+n$ is equal to :
questions.sol:
$A=\begin{bmatrix}0&a&1\\2&0&0\\a&1&1\end{bmatrix}$, so $\det A=-a(2-0)+1(2-0)=2-2a=-4$, giving $a=3$.
Then $\det\left(4\,\mathrm{adj}(2A)\right)$. For a $3\times3$ matrix, $\mathrm{adj}(2A)=2^2\,\mathrm{adj}A$, so this is $\det(16\,\mathrm{adj}A)=16^3(\det A)^2=2^{12}\cdot16=2^{16}$.
So $m=16$, $n=0$ and $m+n=16$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left(\dfrac{(x+1)}{\left(x^{2/3}+1-x^{1/3}\right)}-\dfrac{(x-1)}{\left(x-x^{1/2}\right)}\right)^{10}$, $x>1$, is :
questions.sol:
$x+1=\left(x^{1/3}+1\right)\left(x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1\right)$, so the first fraction is $x^{1/3}+1$.
$\dfrac{x-1}{x-x^{1/2}}=\dfrac{(\sqrt x-1)(\sqrt x+1)}{\sqrt x(\sqrt x-1)}=1+x^{-1/2}$.
The expression is $\left(x^{1/3}-x^{-1/2}\right)^{10}$, with general term $\binom{10}{r}(-1)^rx^{\frac{10-r}{3}-\frac r2}$.
$\dfrac{10-r}{3}=\dfrac r2$ gives $r=4$; the term is $\binom{10}{4}=210$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $P_n=\alpha^n+\beta^n$, $n\in\mathbf{N}$. If $P_{10}=123$, $P_9=76$, $P_8=47$ and $P_1=1$, then the quadratic equation having roots $\dfrac1\alpha$ and $\dfrac1\beta$ is :
questions.sol:
With $s=\alpha+\beta=P_1=1$ and $p=\alpha\beta$: $P_{10}=sP_9-pP_8$, so $123=76-47p$ and $p=-1$.
So $\alpha, \beta$ are the roots of $x^2-x-1=0$.
Replacing $x$ by $\dfrac1x$: $1-x-x^2=0$, i.e. $x^2+x-1=0$ has roots $\dfrac1\alpha, \dfrac1\beta$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&-1\\6&\beta\end{bmatrix}$, $\alpha>0$, such that $\det(A)=0$ and $\alpha+\beta=1$. If I denotes $2\times2$ identity matrix, then the matrix $(I+A)^8$ is :
questions.sol:
$\alpha\beta+6=0$ and $\beta=1-\alpha$ give $\alpha^2-\alpha-6=0$, so $\alpha=3$, $\beta=-2$.
$A=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\6&-2\end{bmatrix}$ and $A^2=\begin{bmatrix}3&-1\\6&-2\end{bmatrix}=A$.
Hence $(I+A)^8=I+\left(\binom81+\binom82+\cdots+\binom88\right)A=I+255A=\begin{bmatrix}766&-255\\1530&-509\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.text:
If the system of linear equations
$3x+y+\beta z=3$
$2x+\alpha y-z=-3$
$x+2y+z=4$
has infinitely many solutions, then the value of $22\beta-9\alpha$ is :
questions.sol:
The last two equations are independent, so for infinitely many solutions the first must be a combination $p(\text{second})+q(\text{third})$.
Comparing the $x$ coefficients and constants: $2p+q=3$ and $-3p+4q=3$, so $p=\dfrac9{11}$, $q=\dfrac{15}{11}$.
$y$: $\alpha p+2q=1$ gives $\alpha=-\dfrac{19}{9}$; $z$: $\beta=-p+q=\dfrac6{11}$.
$22\beta-9\alpha=12+19=31$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: If the area of the region $\left\{(x, y): \left|4-x^2\right|\le y\le x^2, y\le4, x\ge0\right\}$ is $\left(\dfrac{80\sqrt2}{\alpha}-\beta\right)$, $\alpha, \beta\in\mathbf{N}$, then $\alpha+\beta$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
$|4-x^2|\le x^2$ needs $x\ge\sqrt2$; $x^2-4\le y\le4$ needs $x\le2\sqrt2$.
For $\sqrt2\le x\le2$: $4-x^2\le y\le x^2$, area $\displaystyle\int_{\sqrt2}^{2}(2x^2-4)\,dx=\frac{8\sqrt2-8}{3}$.
For $2\le x\le2\sqrt2$: $x^2-4\le y\le4$, area $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{2\sqrt2}(8-x^2)\,dx=\frac{32\sqrt2-40}{3}$.
Total $=\dfrac{40\sqrt2}{3}-16=\dfrac{80\sqrt2}{6}-16$, so $\alpha=6$, $\beta=16$ and $\alpha+\beta=22$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The absolute difference between the squares of the radii of the two circles passing through the point $(-9, 4)$ and touching the lines $x+y=3$ and $x-y=3$, is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
The centre lies on a bisector of the two lines: $y=0$ or $x=3$.
Centre $(h, 0)$, radius $\dfrac{|h-3|}{\sqrt2}$: $(h+9)^2+16=\dfrac{(h-3)^2}{2}$ gives $h^2+42h+185=0$, so $h=-5$ or $-37$, with $r^2=32$ or $800$.
Centre $(3, k)$: $144+(k-4)^2=\dfrac{k^2}{2}$ gives $k^2-16k+320=0$, which has no real roots.
Difference $=800-32=768$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $[\cdot]$ denote the greatest integer function. If $\displaystyle\int_0^{e^3}\left[\frac{1}{e^{x-1}}\right]dx=\alpha-\log_e2$, then $\alpha^3$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
The integrand is $\left[e^{1-x}\right]$, which decreases from $e$.
It equals 2 for $0\le x<1-\log_e2$, 1 for $1-\log_e2\le x<1$, and 0 for $x>1$.
Integral $=2(1-\log_e2)+\log_e2=2-\log_e2$, so $\alpha=2$ and $\alpha^3=8$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Let $f:\mathbf{R}\to\mathbf{R}$ be a thrice differentiable odd function satisfying $f^\prime(x)\ge0$, $f^{\prime\prime}(x)=f(x)$, $f(0)=0$, $f^\prime(0)=3$. Then $9f(\log_e3)$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
Multiply $f^{\prime\prime}=f$ by $2f^\prime$ and integrate: $(f^\prime)^2-f^2=9$ (using $f(0)=0$, $f^\prime(0)=3$).
With $f^\prime\ge0$: $\dfrac{df}{\sqrt{9+f^2}}=dx$, so $\log\left(f+\sqrt{9+f^2}\right)=x+\log3$, giving $f(x)=\dfrac32\left(e^x-e^{-x}\right)$ (odd, as required).
$f(\log_e3)=\dfrac32\left(3-\dfrac13\right)=4$, so $9f(\log_e3)=36$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: Three distinct numbers are selected randomly from the set $\{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 40\}$. If the probability, that the selected numbers are in an increasing G.P., is $\dfrac mn$, $\gcd(m, n)=1$, then $m+n$ is equal to __________.
questions.sol:
An increasing G.P. of integers with ratio $\dfrac pq$ ($p>q$, coprime) has the form $kq^2, kpq, kp^2$ with $kp^2\le40$.
$p=2$ ($q=1$): 10; $p=3$ ($q=1, 2$): $2\times4=8$; $p=4$ ($q=1, 3$): $2\times2=4$; $p=5$ ($q=1,2,3,4$): 4; $p=6$ ($q=1, 5$): 2. Total 28.
Probability $=\dfrac{28}{\binom{40}{3}}=\dfrac{28}{9880}=\dfrac{7}{2470}$, so $m+n=2477$.
questions.subject: Mathematics

questions.text: The equation for real gas is given by $\left(P+\dfrac{a}{V^2}\right)(V-b)=RT$, where P, V, T and R are the pressure, volume, temperature and gas constant, respectively. The dimension of $ab^{-2}$ is equivalent to that of :
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{a}{V^2}$ has the dimensions of pressure, so $[a]=[PV^2]$; $b$ has the dimensions of volume.
$[ab^{-2}]=[P]=[\mathrm{ML^{-1}T^{-2}}]$, the same as energy per unit volume, i.e. energy density.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Match List - I with List - II.
List - IList - II
(A) Coefficient of viscosity(I) $[\mathrm{ML^0T^{-3}}]$
(B) Intensity of wave(II) $[\mathrm{ML^{-2}T^{-2}}]$
(C) Pressure gradient(III) $[\mathrm{M^{-1}LT^2}]$
(D) Compressibility(IV) $[\mathrm{ML^{-1}T^{-1}}]$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) Viscosity: $\dfrac{F}{A\,(dv/dx)}$ has $[\mathrm{ML^{-1}T^{-1}}]$ (IV).
(B) Intensity is power per unit area: $\dfrac{\mathrm{ML^2T^{-3}}}{\mathrm{L^2}}=[\mathrm{ML^0T^{-3}}]$ (I).
(C) Pressure gradient: $\dfrac{\mathrm{ML^{-1}T^{-2}}}{\mathrm{L}}=[\mathrm{ML^{-2}T^{-2}}]$ (II).
(D) Compressibility is the reciprocal of bulk modulus: $[\mathrm{M^{-1}LT^2}]$ (III).

questions.text: A cord of negligible mass is wound around the rim of a wheel supported by spokes with negligible mass. The mass of wheel is 10 kg and radius is 10 cm and it can freely rotate without any friction. Initially the wheel is at rest. If a steady pull of 20 N is applied on the cord, the angular velocity of the wheel, after the cord is unwound by 1 m, would be :
questions.sol:
With massless spokes the wheel is a ring: $I=MR^2=10\times(0.1)^2=0.1$ kg m$^2$.
Work done by the pull $=20\times1=20$ J $=\dfrac12I\omega^2$.
$\omega^2=\dfrac{40}{0.1}=400$, so $\omega=20$ rad/s.

questions.text: A river is flowing from west to east direction with speed of 9 km h$^{-1}$. If a boat capable of moving at a maximum speed of 27 km h$^{-1}$ in still water, crosses the river in half a minute, while moving with maximum speed at an angle of $150^\circ$ to direction of river flow, then the width of the river is :
questions.sol:
Only the component of the boat's velocity (relative to water) across the river carries it across: $27\sin150^\circ=13.5$ km h$^{-1}=3.75$ m s$^{-1}$.
Width $=3.75\times30=112.5$ m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A square Lamina OABC of length 10 cm is pivoted at 'O'. Forces act at Lamina as shown in figure. If Lamina remains stationary, then the magnitude of F is :
questions.sol:
Take moments about O (anticlockwise positive), with O at the origin, A at $(10, 0)$, B at $(10, 10)$ and C at $(0, 10)$ in cm.
At C: the upward 10 N passes through O's vertical line (zero moment); F to the left gives $+10F$.
At B: upward 10 N gives $+100$; rightward 10 N gives $-100$.
At A: rightward 10 N has zero moment; downward 10 N gives $-100$.
Equilibrium: $10F+100-100-100=0$, so $F=10$ N (the pivot supplies the balancing force).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion

questions.text: In an adiabatic process, which of the following statements is true ?
options: Work done by the gas equals the increase in internal energy
The internal energy of the gas decreases as the temperature increases
The molar heat capacity is zero
The molar heat capacity is infinite
questions.sol:
In an adiabatic process no heat is exchanged, so $C=\dfrac{\Delta Q}{n\Delta T}=0$ although the temperature changes.
Work done by the gas equals the decrease (not increase) in internal energy, and internal energy of an ideal gas rises with temperature.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Moment of inertia of a rod of mass 'M' and length 'L' about an axis passing through its center and normal to its length is '$\alpha$'. Now the rod is cut into two equal parts and these parts are joined symmetrically to form a cross shape. Moment of inertia of cross about an axis passing through its center and normal to plane containing cross is :
questions.sol:
$\alpha=\dfrac{ML^2}{12}$.
Each half has mass $\dfrac M2$ and length $\dfrac L2$, and is centred on the axis: $I=\dfrac{1}{12}\cdot\dfrac M2\cdot\dfrac{L^2}{4}=\dfrac{ML^2}{96}$.
Cross: $2\times\dfrac{ML^2}{96}=\dfrac{ML^2}{48}=\dfrac\alpha4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A particle is subjected to two simple harmonic motions as :
$x_1=\sqrt7\sin5t$ cm
and $x_2=2\sqrt7\sin\left(5t+\dfrac\pi3\right)$ cm
where $x$ is displacement and $t$ is time in seconds.
The maximum acceleration of the particle is $x\times10^{-2}$ m s$^{-2}$. The value of $x$ is :
questions.sol:
Resultant amplitude: $A^2=7+28+2\cdot\sqrt7\cdot2\sqrt7\cos60^\circ=49$, so $A=7$ cm.
$a_{\max}=\omega^2A=25\times7=175$ cm s$^{-2}=175\times10^{-2}$ m s$^{-2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A small bob of mass 100 mg and charge $+10\ \mu$C is connected to an insulating string of length 1 m. It is brought near to an infinitely long non-conducting sheet of charge density '$\sigma$' as shown in figure. If string subtends an angle of $45^\circ$ with the sheet at equilibrium the charge density of sheet will be.
(Given, $\epsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}\ \dfrac{\mathrm{F}}{\mathrm{m}}$ and acceleration due to gravity, $g=10\ \dfrac{\mathrm{m}}{\mathrm{s^2}}$)
questions.sol:
At equilibrium $\tan45^\circ=\dfrac{qE}{mg}$, so $qE=mg=100\times10^{-6}\times10=10^{-3}$ N.
$E=\dfrac{10^{-3}}{10\times10^{-6}}=100$ N/C $=\dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}$.
$\sigma=200\times8.85\times10^{-12}=1.77\times10^{-9}$ C/m$^2=1.77$ nC/m$^2$.

questions.text: The battery of a mobile phone is rated as 4.2 V, 5800 mAh. How much energy is stored in it when fully charged ?
questions.sol:
Charge $=5.8\ \mathrm{A}\times3600\ \mathrm{s}=20880$ C.
Energy $=VQ=4.2\times20880\approx87700$ J $=87.7$ kJ.

questions.text:
The relationship between the magnetic susceptibility ($\chi$) and the magnetic permeability ($\mu$) is given by :
($\mu_0$ is the permeability of free space and $\mu_r$ is relative permeability)
questions.sol: $\mu=\mu_0(1+\chi)$, so $\mu_r=\dfrac{\mu}{\mu_0}=1+\chi$ and $\chi=\dfrac{\mu}{\mu_0}-1$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Consider two infinitely large plane parallel conducting plates as shown below. The plates are uniformly charged with a surface charge density $+\sigma$ and $-2\sigma$. The force experienced by a point charge $+q$ placed at the mid point between two plates will be :
questions.sol:
Treat each plate as a large charged sheet. Between the plates, the field of the $+\sigma$ plate ($\dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}$, away from it) and that of the $-2\sigma$ plate ($\dfrac{2\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}$, towards it) point the same way.
$E=\dfrac{\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}+\dfrac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0}=\dfrac{3\sigma}{2\epsilon_0}$, so $F=\dfrac{3\sigma q}{2\epsilon_0}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: Let $B_1$ be the magnitude of magnetic field at center of a circular coil of radius R carrying current I. Let $B_2$ be the magnitude of magnetic field at an axial distance '$x$' from the center. For $x : R=3 : 4$, $\dfrac{B_2}{B_1}$ is :
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A point charge $+q$ is placed at the origin. A second point charge $+9q$ is placed at $(d, 0, 0)$ in Cartesian coordinate system. The point in between them where the electric field vanishes is :
questions.sol: At $(x, 0, 0)$ with $0<x<d$: $\dfrac{q}{x^2}=\dfrac{9q}{(d-x)^2}$, so $d-x=3x$ and $x=\dfrac d4$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A light wave is propagating with plane wave fronts of the type $x+y+z=$ constant. The angle made by the direction of wave propagation with the $x$-axis is :
questions.sol:
The light travels along the normal to the planes of constant phase, i.e. along $\hat i+\hat j+\hat k$.
Its direction cosine with the $x$-axis is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}$, so the angle is $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\right)$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A slanted object AB is placed on one side of convex lens as shown in the diagram. The image is formed on the opposite side. Angle made by the image with principal axis is :
questions.sol:
A is on the axis at $u=-30$ cm; B is 1 cm nearer the lens and 2 cm above the axis.
Image of A: $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1{20}-\dfrac1{30}$, $v=60$ cm.
Image of B ($u=-29$ cm): $\dfrac1v=\dfrac1{20}-\dfrac1{29}$, $v\approx64.4$ cm, magnification $\approx-2.22$, so it is about 4.4 cm below the axis.
The image runs about 4.4 cm along the axis and 4.4 cm below it (for small objects: longitudinal magnification $m^2=4$, transverse $m=-2$, giving 4 cm and $-4$ cm), so it makes $-45^\circ$ with the principal axis.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A spherical surface separates two media of refractive indices 1 and 1.5 as shown in figure. Distance of the image of an object 'O', is :
(C is the center of curvature of the spherical surface and R is the radius of curvature)
options: 0.4 m left to the spherical surface
0.4 m right to the spherical surface
0.24 m left to the spherical surface
0.24 m right to the spherical surface
questions.sol:
Light goes from medium 1 to medium 2; $u=-0.2$ m and $R=+0.4$ m (C is on the far side).
$\dfrac{n_2}{v}-\dfrac{n_1}{u}=\dfrac{n_2-n_1}{R}$: $\dfrac{1.5}{v}+5=1.25$, so $v=-0.4$ m.
The image is virtual, 0.4 m to the left of the surface.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Considering Bohr's atomic model for hydrogen atom :
(A) the energy of H atom in ground state is same as energy of He$^+$ ion in its first excited state.
(B) the energy of H atom in ground state is same as that for Li$^{++}$ ion in its second excited state.
(C) the energy of H atom in its ground state is same as that of He$^+$ ion for its ground state.
(D) the energy of He$^+$ ion in its first excited state is same as that for Li$^{++}$ ion in its ground state.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
$E_n=-13.6\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$ eV, so compare $\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}$. H ground state: 1.
(A) He$^+$, $n=2$: $\dfrac44=1$. True.
(B) Li$^{++}$, $n=3$: $\dfrac99=1$. True.
(C) He$^+$, $n=1$: 4. False.
(D) He$^+$, $n=2$: 1, but Li$^{++}$, $n=1$: 9. False.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A monochromatic light is incident on a metallic plate having work function $\phi$. An electron, emitted normally to the plate from a point A with maximum kinetic energy, enters a constant magnetic field, perpendicular to the initial velocity of electron. The electron passes through a curve and hits back the plate at a point B. The distance between A and B is :
(Given : The magnitude of charge of an electron is e and mass is m, h is Planck's constant and c is velocity of light. Take the magnetic field exists throughout the path of electron)
questions.sol:
$K_{\max}=\dfrac{hc}{\lambda}-\phi$ and $mv=\sqrt{2mK_{\max}}$.
The electron describes a semicircle of radius $r=\dfrac{mv}{eB}$ and lands a diameter away: $AB=2r=\dfrac{2\sqrt{2mK_{\max}}}{eB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{8m\left(\frac{hc}{\lambda}-\phi\right)}}{eB}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter

questions.text: A zener diode with 5 V zener voltage is used to regulate an unregulated dc voltage input of 25 V. For a 400 $\Omega$ resistor connected in series, the zener current is found to be 4 times load current. The load current ($I_L$) and load resistance ($R_L$) are :
questions.sol:
Current in the series resistor $=\dfrac{25-5}{400}=0.05$ A $=I_Z+I_L=5I_L$.
$I_L=10$ mA and $R_L=\dfrac{5}{0.01}=500\ \Omega$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A steel wire of length 2 m and Young's modulus $2.0\times10^{11}$ N m$^{-2}$ is stretched by a force. If Poisson ratio and transverse strain for the wire are 0.2 and $10^{-3}$ respectively, then the elastic potential energy density of the wire is __________ $\times10^5$ (in SI units).
questions.sol:
Longitudinal strain $=\dfrac{10^{-3}}{0.2}=5\times10^{-3}$.
Energy density $=\dfrac12Y(\text{strain})^2=\dfrac12\times2\times10^{11}\times25\times10^{-6}=25\times10^5$ J m$^{-3}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
A vessel with square cross-section and height of 6 m is vertically partitioned. A small window of 100 cm$^2$ with hinged door is fitted at a depth of 3 m in the partition wall. One part of the vessel is filled completely with water and the other side is filled with the liquid having density $1.5\times10^3$ kg/m$^3$. What force one needs to apply on the hinged door so that it does not get opened ?
(Acceleration due to gravity $=10$ m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
At a depth of 3 m the pressure difference across the partition is $(1500-1000)\times10\times3=1.5\times10^4$ Pa.
Net force on the door $=1.5\times10^4\times100\times10^{-4}=150$ N, so a force of 150 N is needed.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: $\gamma_A$ is the specific heat ratio of monoatomic gas A having 3 translational degrees of freedom. $\gamma_B$ is the specific heat ratio of polyatomic gas B having 3 translational, 3 rotational degrees of freedom and 1 vibrational mode. If $\dfrac{\gamma_A}{\gamma_B}=\left(1+\dfrac1n\right)$, then the value of n is __________.
questions.sol:
$\gamma_A=1+\dfrac23=\dfrac53$.
For B a vibrational mode contributes 2 (kinetic and potential), so $f=3+3+2=8$ and $\gamma_B=1+\dfrac28=\dfrac54$.
$\dfrac{\gamma_A}{\gamma_B}=\dfrac43=1+\dfrac13$, so $n=3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A person travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity $v_1$ for a distance $x$ and with a uniform velocity $v_2$ for the next $\dfrac32x$ distance. The average velocity in this motion is $\dfrac{50}{7}$ m/s. If $v_1$ is 5 m/s then $v_2=$ __________ m/s.
questions.sol:
Total time $=\dfrac x5+\dfrac{1.5x}{v_2}$ and total distance $=2.5x$.
$\dfrac{2.5x}{50/7}=0.35x$, so $\dfrac{1.5}{v_2}=0.35-0.2=0.15$ and $v_2=10$ m/s.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: If the measured angular separation between the second minimum to the left of the central maximum and the third minimum to the right of the central maximum is $30^\circ$ in a single slit diffraction pattern recorded using 628 nm light, then the width of the slit is __________ $\mu$m.
questions.sol:
Minima lie at angles $\theta_n\approx\dfrac{n\lambda}{a}$ on either side of the centre, so the separation is $(2+3)\dfrac\lambda a=\dfrac{5\lambda}{a}$.
$\dfrac{5\lambda}{a}=\dfrac\pi6$ gives $a=\dfrac{30\lambda}{\pi}=\dfrac{30\times628\ \mathrm{nm}}{3.14}=6000$ nm $=6\ \mu$m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
$\mathrm{CaCO_3(s)+2HCl(aq)\rightarrow CaCl_2(aq)+CO_2(g)+H_2O(l)}$
Consider the above reaction, what mass of $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ will be formed if 250 mL of 0.76 M HCl reacts with 1000 g of $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ ?
(Given : Molar mass of Ca, C, O, H and Cl are 40, 12, 16, 1 and 35.5 g mol$^{-1}$, respectively)
questions.sol:
HCl $=0.250\times0.76=0.19$ mol; 1000 g of $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ is 10 mol, a large excess, so HCl is limiting.
$\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ formed $=\dfrac{0.19}{2}=0.095$ mol $\times111$ g mol$^{-1}=10.545$ g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: According to Bohr's model of hydrogen atom, which of the following statement is incorrect ?
options: Radius of 4$^{\text{th}}$ orbit is four times larger than that of 2$^{\text{nd}}$ orbit
Radius of 6$^{\text{th}}$ orbit is three times larger than that of 4$^{\text{th}}$ orbit
Radius of 8$^{\text{th}}$ orbit is four times larger than that of 4$^{\text{th}}$ orbit
Radius of 3$^{\text{rd}}$ orbit is nine times larger than that of 1$^{\text{st}}$ orbit
questions.sol:
$r_n\propto n^2$.
$\dfrac{r_4}{r_2}=4$, $\dfrac{r_8}{r_4}=4$, $\dfrac{r_3}{r_1}=9$, but $\dfrac{r_6}{r_4}=\dfrac{36}{16}=2.25$, not 3.
The incorrect statement is the one about the 6th and 4th orbits.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Two vessels A and B are connected via stopcock. The vessel A is filled with a gas at a certain pressure. The entire assembly is immersed in water and is allowed to come to thermal equilibrium with water. After opening the stopcock the gas from vessel A expands into vessel B and no change in temperature is observed in the thermometer. Which of the following statement is true ?
options: The pressure in the vessel B before opening the stopcock is zero
questions.sol:
This is free expansion of a gas into an evacuated vessel (Joule's experiment): B is under vacuum, so the gas expands against zero pressure.
Hence $dw=0$; no temperature change means $dq=0$ and $dU=0$.
The true statement is that the pressure in B before opening the stopcock is zero.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Which of the following graph correctly represents the plots of $K_H$ at 1 bar for gases in water versus temperature?
questions.sol:
A larger $K_H$ means a less soluble gas. Among the gases shown, He is the least soluble (largest $K_H$), then $\mathrm{N_2}$, then $\mathrm{O_2}$, with $\mathrm{CH_4}$ far more soluble (smallest $K_H$).
For such gases $K_H$ first rises with temperature and then falls, giving curves with a maximum.
So the correct plot has the curves in the order He above $\mathrm{N_2}$ above $\mathrm{CH_4}$ (option 2). The plot with $\mathrm{O_2}$ on top is wrong, and the straight-line and U-shaped plots do not match the observed behaviour.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A solution is made by mixing one mole of volatile liquid A with 3 moles of volatile liquid B. The vapour pressure of pure A is 200 mm Hg and that of the solution is 500 mm Hg. The vapour pressure of pure B and the least volatile component of the solution, respectively, are :
questions.sol:
$x_A=0.25$, $x_B=0.75$. Raoult's law: $500=0.25\times200+0.75\,p_B^\circ$, so $p_B^\circ=600$ mm Hg.
A has the lower vapour pressure (200 mm Hg), so A is the less volatile component.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
If equal volumes of $\mathrm{AB_2}$ and XY (both are salts) aqueous solutions are mixed, which of the following combination will give a precipitate of $\mathrm{AY_2}$ at 300 K ?
(Given $K_{sp}$ (at 300 K) for $\mathrm{AY_2}=5.2\times10^{-7}$)
questions.sol:
Mixing equal volumes halves each concentration; precipitation needs $Q=[\mathrm{A^{2+}}][\mathrm{Y^-}]^2>K_{sp}$.
Option 1: $(10^{-2})(10^{-2})^2=10^{-6}>5.2\times10^{-7}$. Precipitate forms.
Option 2: $(7.5\times10^{-5})(7.5\times10^{-4})^2\approx4.2\times10^{-11}$; option 3: $(10^{-4})(4\times10^{-4})^2=1.6\times10^{-11}$; option 4: $(1.8\times10^{-3})(2.5\times10^{-4})^2\approx1.1\times10^{-10}$. All below $K_{sp}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Among $\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{XeF_2}$, $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ and $\mathrm{SF_4}$, the hybridization of the molecule with non-zero dipole moment and highest number of lone-pairs of electrons on the central atom is :
questions.sol:
Lone pairs on the central atom: $\mathrm{SO_2}$ 1, $\mathrm{NF_3}$ 1, $\mathrm{NH_3}$ 1, $\mathrm{XeF_2}$ 3, $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ 2, $\mathrm{SF_4}$ 1.
$\mathrm{XeF_2}$ is linear and non-polar, so among the polar molecules $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ (T-shaped, 2 lone pairs) has the most.
Cl has 5 electron pairs: $sp^3d$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
The property/properties that show irregularity in first four elements of group-17 is/are :
(A) Covalent radius
(B) Electron affinity
(C) Ionic radius
(D) First ionization energy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
From F to I the covalent and ionic radii increase steadily and the first ionisation energy decreases steadily.
Electron gain enthalpy is irregular: Cl has the most negative value, more than F, because the small, crowded 2p shell of F repels the incoming electron.
So only (B) shows irregularity.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The metallic radius of Al is less than that of Ga.
Statement (II) : The ionic radius of $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ is less than that of $\mathrm{Ga^{3+}}$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Metallic radius: Al 143 pm, Ga 135 pm; the poorly shielding 3d electrons in Ga make it smaller. Statement I is incorrect.
Ionic radius: $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ about 54 pm, $\mathrm{Ga^{3+}}$ about 62 pm. Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : In octahedral complexes, when $\Delta_o<P$ high spin complexes are formed. When $\Delta_o>P$ low spin complexes are formed.
Statement (II) : In tetrahedral complexes because of $\Delta_t<P$, low spin complexes are rarely formed.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
If the splitting is smaller than the pairing energy, electrons occupy the upper $e_g$ set before pairing (high spin); if larger, they pair in $t_{2g}$ (low spin). Statement I is correct.
$\Delta_t\approx\dfrac49\Delta_o$ is usually smaller than P, so tetrahedral complexes are almost always high spin. Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A molecule with the formula $\mathrm{AX_4Y}$ has all it's elements from p-block. Element A is rarest, monoatomic, non-radioactive from its group and has the lowest ionization enthalpy value among A, X and Y. Elements X and Y have first and second highest electronegativity values respectively among all the known elements. The shape of the molecule is :
questions.sol:
A is a noble gas (monoatomic); the rarest non-radioactive one is xenon. X is F and Y is O, so the molecule is $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$.
Xe has 6 electron pairs (5 bonding domains and 1 lone pair): octahedral arrangement with one position taken by the lone pair, i.e. square pyramidal.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Choose the correct tests with respective observations.
(A) $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ (acidified with acetic acid) $+\ \mathrm{K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\rightarrow$ Chocolate brown precipitate.
(B) $\mathrm{FeCl_3+K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\rightarrow$ Prussian blue precipitate.
(C) $\mathrm{ZnCl_2+K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$, neutralised with $\mathrm{NH_4OH}\rightarrow$ White or bluish white precipitate.
(D) $\mathrm{MgCl_2+K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}\rightarrow$ Blue precipitate.
(E) $\mathrm{BaCl_2+K_4[Fe(CN)_6]}$, neutralised with NaOH $\rightarrow$ White precipitate.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
(A) $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ gives chocolate-brown $\mathrm{Cu_2[Fe(CN)_6]}$. Correct.
(B) $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ gives Prussian blue $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3}$. Correct.
(C) $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$ gives white or bluish-white zinc ferrocyanide. Correct.
(D) and (E): ferrocyanide is not the test for $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ or $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$, and these observations are not obtained.
Answer: A, B and C only.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
On complete combustion 1.0 g of an organic compound (X) gave 1.46 g of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and 0.567 g of $\mathrm{H_2O}$. The empirical formula mass of compound (X) is __________g.
(Given molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ C : 12, H : 1, O : 16 )
questions.sol:
C: $1.46\times\dfrac{12}{44}=0.398$ g ($0.0332$ mol). H: $0.567\times\dfrac{2}{18}=0.063$ g ($0.063$ mol).
O (by difference): $1.0-0.398-0.063=0.539$ g ($0.0337$ mol).
C : H : O $\approx1:2:1$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{CH_2O}$, mass 30 g.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following compound (X)
The most stable and least stable carbon radicals, respectively, produced by homolytic cleavage of corresponding $\mathrm{C-H}$ bond are :
questions.sol:
Removing H from carbon II gives a propargylic radical, stabilised by delocalisation over the triple bond: the most stable.
Carbon III gives a tertiary radical and carbon IV a primary radical.
Removing H from the sp carbon I gives an alkynyl ($\sigma$, sp) radical, which is the least stable.
Answer: II, I.

questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques

questions.text: Designate whether each of the following compounds is aromatic or not aromatic.
options: b, e, f, g aromatic and a, c, d, h not aromatic
a, c, d, e, h aromatic and b, f, g not aromatic
a, b, c, d aromatic and e, f, g, h not aromatic
e, g aromatic and a, b, c, d, f, h not aromatic
questions.sol:
Count the $\pi$ electrons in each planar, fully conjugated ring (Hückel: $4n+2$ is aromatic).
(a) cyclopentadienyl anion, 6: aromatic. (b) cyclopentadienyl cation, 4: not aromatic.
(c) cyclobutadiene dication, 2: aromatic. (d) cyclobutadiene dianion, 6: aromatic.
(e) tropylium cation, 6: aromatic. (f) cyclooctatetraene, 8 and non-planar: not aromatic.
(g) cyclobutadiene, 4: not aromatic. (h) cyclopropenyl cation, 2: aromatic.

questions.text: An optically active alkyl halide $\mathrm{C_4H_9Br}$ [A] reacts with hot KOH dissolved in ethanol and forms alkene [B] as major product which reacts with bromine to give dibromide [C]. The compound [C] is converted into a gas [D] upon reacting with alcoholic $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$. During hydration 18 gram of water is added to 1 mole of gas [D] on warming with mercuric sulphate and dilute acid at 333 K to form compound [E]. The IUPAC name of compound [E] is :
questions.sol:
The only chiral $\mathrm{C_4H_9Br}$ is 2-bromobutane [A]. Dehydrohalogenation gives mainly but-2-ene [B] (Saytzeff); bromine gives 2,3-dibromobutane [C].
Double dehydrobromination gives but-2-yne [D], a gas.
Hydration ($\mathrm{Hg^{2+}}$, dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$) of but-2-yne gives the enol, which tautomerises to butan-2-one [E].
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following molecules :
The correct order of rate of hydrolysis is :
questions.sol:
The reactivity of acyl compounds towards nucleophilic attack falls as the leaving group becomes poorer and as the lone pair on the attached atom donates more strongly to C=O.
Acid chloride (p) > anhydride (q) > ester (r) > amide (s).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : Vanillin (structure shown in the figure) will react with NaOH and also with Tollen's reagent.
Statement (II) : Vanillin (structure shown in the figure) will undergo self aldol condensation very easily.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Vanillin has a phenolic OH (acidic, so it reacts with NaOH) and a CHO group (oxidised by Tollens' reagent). Statement I is correct.
The CHO group is attached directly to the ring, so there is no $\alpha$-hydrogen and self aldol condensation is not possible. Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: The correct order of basic nature in aqueous solution for the bases $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2N-NH_2}$, $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$, $\mathrm{(CH_3CH_2)_2NH}$ and $\mathrm{(CH_3CH_2)_3N}$ is :
questions.sol:
Hydrazine is a weaker base than ammonia (the electron-withdrawing adjacent N); ethylamines are stronger than ammonia.
In water, for ethyl amines the combined inductive, solvation and steric effects give $\mathrm{(C_2H_5)_2NH>(C_2H_5)_3N>C_2H_5NH_2}$.
Order: $\mathrm{N_2H_4<NH_3<C_2H_5NH_2<(C_2H_5)_3N<(C_2H_5)_2NH}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: Identify the correct statement among the following :
options: All naturally occurring amino acids except glycine contain one chiral centre.
All naturally occurring amino acids are optically active.
Amino acid, cysteine can easily undergo dimerisation due to the presence of free SH group.
Glutamic acid is the only amino acid that contains a $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group at the side chain.
questions.sol:
Option 1 is wrong: threonine and isoleucine have two chiral centres. Option 2 is wrong: glycine is optically inactive.
Option 4 is wrong: aspartic acid also has a side-chain COOH.
Cysteine's SH groups are readily oxidised to an S$-$S link, joining two molecules as cystine. Option 3 is correct.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following electrochemical cell at standard condition.
$\mathrm{Au(s)\,|\,QH_2, Q\,|\,NH_4X(0.01\ M)\,||\,Ag^+(1\ M)\,|\,Ag(s)}$ $\quad E_{\text{cell}}=+0.4$ V
The couple $\mathrm{QH_2/Q}$ represents quinhydrone electrode, the half cell reaction is given below :
$\left[\text{Given : } E^\circ_{\mathrm{Ag^+/Ag}}=+0.8\ \text{V and } \dfrac{2.303RT}{F}=0.06\ \text{V}\right]$
The $\mathrm{p}K_b$ value of the ammonium halide salt ($\mathrm{NH_4X}$) used here is __________. (nearest integer)
questions.sol:
For $\mathrm{Q+2H^++2e^-\rightarrow QH_2}$: $E=0.7-\dfrac{0.06}{2}\log\dfrac{1}{[\mathrm{H^+}]^2}=0.7-0.06\,\mathrm{pH}$.
$E_{\text{cell}}=E_{\text{cathode}}-E_{\text{anode}}=0.8-(0.7-0.06\,\mathrm{pH})=0.4$, so $\mathrm{pH}=5$.
For the salt of a weak base and strong acid: $\mathrm{pH}=7-\dfrac12\mathrm{p}K_b-\dfrac12\log C=7-\dfrac12\mathrm{p}K_b+1$.
$5=8-\dfrac12\mathrm{p}K_b$, so $\mathrm{p}K_b=6$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
For the reaction A $\rightarrow$ products.
The concentration of A at 10 minutes is __________ $\times10^{-3}$ mol L$^{-1}$ (nearest integer). The reaction was started with 2.5 mol L$^{-1}$ of A.
questions.sol:
$t_{1/2}\propto[\mathrm{A}]_0$ (straight line through the origin), so the reaction is zero order with $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{A}]_0}{2k}$.
Slope $=\dfrac1{2k}=76.92$ min L mol$^{-1}$, so $k=\dfrac{1}{153.84}=0.0065$ mol L$^{-1}$ min$^{-1}$.
$[\mathrm{A}]=2.5-0.0065\times10=2.435$ mol L$^{-1}=2435\times10^{-3}$ mol L$^{-1}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text:
Consider the following equilibrium,
$\mathrm{CO(g)+2H_2(g)\rightleftharpoons CH_3OH(g)}$
0.1 mol of CO along with a catalyst is present in a 2 dm$^3$ flask maintained at 500 K. Hydrogen is introduced into the flask until the pressure is 5 bar and 0.04 mol of $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$ is formed. The $K_p^\theta$ is __________ $\times10^{-3}$ (nearest integer).
Given : R $=0.08$ dm$^3$ bar K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$
Assume only methanol is formed as the product and the system follows ideal gas behaviour.
questions.sol:
Total moles at equilibrium $=\dfrac{PV}{RT}=\dfrac{5\times2}{0.08\times500}=0.25$.
CO $=0.1-0.04=0.06$, $\mathrm{CH_3OH}=0.04$, so $\mathrm{H_2}=0.25-0.10=0.15$ mol.
Partial pressures: CO $1.2$ bar, $\mathrm{H_2}$ $3$ bar, $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$ $0.8$ bar.
$K_p=\dfrac{0.8}{1.2\times3^2}=0.0741=74\times10^{-3}$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.text: A transition metal (M) among Mn, Cr, Co and Fe has the highest standard electrode potential $\left(\mathrm{M^{3+}/M^{2+}}\right)$. It forms a metal complex of the type $\mathrm{[M(CN)_6]^{4-}}$. The number of electrons present in the $e_g$ orbital of the complex is __________.
questions.sol:
$E^\circ(\mathrm{M^{3+}/M^{2+}})$: Cr $-0.41$, Mn $+1.57$, Fe $+0.77$, Co $+1.97$ V, so M is Co.
In $\mathrm{[Co(CN)_6]^{4-}}$, Co is $+2$ ($3d^7$); $\mathrm{CN^-}$ is a strong-field ligand, giving $t_{2g}^6e_g^1$.
Electrons in $e_g$ $=1$.

questions.text:
0.1 mol of the following given antiviral compound (P) will weigh __________ $\times10^{-1}$ g (nearest integer).
(Given : molar mass in g mol$^{-1}$ H : 1, C : 12, N : 14, O : 16, F : 19, I : 127)
questions.sol:
The base is 5-iodouracil ($\mathrm{C_4H_2IN_2O_2}$ as attached, with N$-$H) and the sugar part is $\mathrm{C_5H_8FO_3}$ (two OH groups, ring O, F on C-2$^\prime$).
Molecular formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}FIN_2O_5}$: $108+10+19+127+28+80=372$ g mol$^{-1}$.
0.1 mol weighs 37.2 g $=372\times10^{-1}$ g.
